function_description: Compute the maximum of elements over one or more array axes.
code_example:
import jax.lax
import jax.numpy as jnp
result = jax.lax.reduce_max(jnp.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]]), axis=1)
print(result)

function_description: Splits an array along a specified axis into multiple arrays of given sizes.
code_example:
import jax.numpy as jnp
result = jax.lax.split(jnp.arange(10), sizes=[3, 3, 4], axis=0)
parameters: operand (ArrayLike): an array to split
sizes (Sequence[int]): the sizes of the split arrays. The sum of the sizes must be equal to the size of the axis dimension of operand.
axis (int): the axis along which to split the array.

function_description: Computes the minimum of elements over one or more array axes.
code_example:
import jax.lax
import jax.numpy as jnp
result = jax.lax.reduce_min(jnp.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]]), axes=(0,))
note: jax.numpy.min() provides a more flexible NumPy-style min-reduction API built around this function. Other low-level jax.lax reduction operators include reduce_sum, reduce_prod, reduce_max, reduce_and, reduce_or, and reduce_xor.

function_description: Computes the sum of elements over one or more array axes.
code_example:
import jax.lax as lax
import jax.numpy as jnp
result = lax.reduce_sum(jnp.array([[1,2],[3,4]]), axes=[0])

parameters.name: operand
parameters.description: ArrayLike - array over which to sum. Must have numerical dtype.

parameters.name: axes
parameters.description: Sequence[int] - sequence of zero or more unique integers specifying the axes over which to sum. Each entry must satisfy 0 <= axis < operand.ndim.

return type: Array - An array of the same dtype as operand, with shape corresponding to the dimensions of operand.shape with axes removed.
note: Unlike jax.numpy.sum(), jax.lax.reduce_sum() does not upcast narrow-width types for accumulation, so sums of 8-bit or 16-bit types may be subject to rounding errors.

function_description: Prevents the compiler from moving operations across the barrier, ensuring specific execution order and preventing common subexpression elimination and fusion.
parameters: operand: a pytree of JAX values
return type: A pytree of JAX values, with the same structure and contents as operand
note: JAX does not define derivative or batching rules for an optimization barrier. Optimization barriers have no effect outside a compiled function.

function_description: Broadcasts a tree prefix into the structure of a given full tree, replacing leaves in the full tree with those from the prefix.
code_example:
import jax
prefix = (1, 2, 3)
full = (0, {'a': 0, 'b': 0}, (0, 0))
result = jax.tree.broadcast(prefix, full)

function_description: Registers a custom type ID for a foreign function interface (FFI) target.
note: The name must be unique within the process.

function_description: Exports a JAX function for persistent serialization, allowing it to be serialized and rehydrated for use in separate processes.
code_example:
from jax import export
exported = export.export(jnp.sin)(np.arange(4, dtype=np.float32))
parameters: fun_jit (stages.Wrapped) – the function to export. Should be the result of jax.jit.
platforms (Sequence[str] | None) – Optional sequence containing a subset of 'tpu', 'cpu', 'cuda', 'rocm'.
disabled_checks (Sequence[DisabledSafetyCheck]) – the safety checks to disable.
_override_lowering_rules (Sequence[tuple[Any, Any]] | None) – an optional sequence of custom lowering rules for some JAX primitives.
note: The serialized bytes are safe to use in a separate process. The calling convention for multiple platforms is explained in the documentation.

code_example:

p = jr.array([0.2, 0.5, 0.3])

n (RealArray)

shape (Shape or None)

function_description: Customizes dead code elimination (DCE) behavior for a JAX-transformable function by allowing a custom DCE rule.
note: Requires compatibility with jax.jit() and DCE is applied when functions are staged out with jit().

function_description: Computes the product of elements over one or more array axes.
parameters: operand (ArrayLike): array over which to sum. Must have numerical dtype.
axes (Sequence[int]): sequence of zero or more unique integers specifying the axes over which to sum.
note: Unlike jax.numpy.prod(), jax.lax.reduce_prod() does not upcast narrow-width types for accumulation, so products of 8-bit or 16-bit types may be subject to rounding errors.

function_description: Computes the bitwise OR of elements along specified axes of an array.

parameters.name: operand
parameters.description: array over which to compute the reduction. Must have boolean or integer dtype.

parameters.name: axes
parameters.description: sequence of zero or more unique integers specifying the axes over which to reduce. Each entry must satisfy 0 <= axis < operand.ndim.

function_description: Puts values into the destination array by matching 1D index and data slices, returning a modified copy as JAX arrays are immutable.
code_example:
from jax import numpy as jnp
a = jnp.array([[10, 30, 20], [60, 40, 50]])
i = jnp.argmax(a, axis=1, keepdims=True)
b = jnp.put_along_axis(a, i, 99, axis=1, inplace=False)
print(b)
note: The JAX version returns a modified copy of the input array instead of modifying in-place (as numpy.put_along_axis does), requiring the user to set inplace=False.

function_description: Returns the size of the specified mapped axis.
parameters: axis_name

function_description: Computes the bitwise XOR of elements over one or more array axes.
code_example:
import jax.lax as lax
result = lax.reduce_xor(operand=[[1, 2], [3, 4]], axes=(0,))
parameters: operand (ArrayLike): array over which to compute the reduction. Must have boolean or integer dtype.
axes (Sequence[int]): sequence of zero or more unique integers specifying the axes over which to reduce. Each entry must satisfy 0 <= axis < operand.ndim.
note: See also: jax.numpy.bitwise_xor.reduce() for a more flexible NumPy-style logical reduction API, built around jax.lax.reduce_xor(). Other low-level jax.lax reduction operators include jax.lax.reduce_sum(), jax.lax.reduce_prod(), jax.lax.reduce_max(), jax.lax.reduce_min(), jax.lax.reduce_and(), jax.lax.reduce_or().

function_description: Computes the bitwise AND of elements over one or more array axes.
code_example:
import jax.lax as lax
import jax.numpy as jnp
operand = jnp.array([[True, False], [True, True]], dtype=bool)
result = lax.reduce_and(operand, axes=[0])
print(result)
parameters: operand (ArrayLike): array over which to compute the reduction. Must have boolean or integer dtype.
axes (Sequence[int]): sequence of zero or more unique integers specifying the axes over which to reduce. Each entry must satisfy 0 <= axis < operand.ndim.
